stem.en: A flask holds two liquids that mix completely. One boils at 60 °C and the other at 90 °C. The flask is heated slowly. What does the thermometer show?

text.en: A steady rise to 90 °C, because the whole mixture must reach the higher boiling point before anything boils.
The reading stays near 60 °C while the first liquid boils away, then climbs towards 90 °C.
A rise to 75 °C, midway between the two, and then a flat reading until the flask is empty.
A jump to 60 °C, and then a slow fall as the liquid in the flask gets less.

explanation.en: While the liquid with the lower boiling point is boiling, the heat goes into making vapour, so the reading stays near 60 °C. When nearly all of it has gone, the reading climbs towards 90 °C. Option a is wrong because the first liquid boils long before the mixture reaches 90 °C. A mixture like this has no single midway boiling point, as option c claims.

hints.en: Which liquid starts to boil first?
What is the heat used for while a liquid is boiling?
